title: MATH 1365 or MATH 1465 (Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning)
description: A mathematics course on reading and writing proofs: logic, sets, functions, induction, and other proof techniques, often with examples from number theory or combinatorics.
notes: Choice slot: Northeastern's MATH 1365 or the more intensive MATH 1465. Official descriptions are in data/raw/neu/ (courses-2025-26-math page).

title: General Elective
description: Any course the student chooses that counts toward the degree, inside or outside the major.

title: Science Requirement
description: A natural science course with its lab, chosen from an approved list in biology, chemistry, environmental science, mathematics, or physics.

title: Co-op
description: A semester of full-time paid work in the field, arranged through a cooperative education program, with learning goals and a reflection on the experience. It earns no academic credit.
notes: Northeastern co-op term; the plan names no course for it.

title: Computing and Social Issues
description: A course on how computing and technology affect society, such as technology ethics, the law and policy of data, or the history and sociology of technology.
notes: Northeastern: one course from an approved list.

title: Concentration Course
description: An upper-level course in a chosen area of computer science, such as artificial intelligence, systems, software, human-centered computing, or theory.
notes: Northeastern: four courses in one concentration.

title: ENGW 3302 or ENGW 3315 (Advanced Writing in the Technical Professions)
description: An advanced writing course on professional and technical documents, such as reports, proposals, and instructions, written for specific audiences.
notes: Choice slot: Northeastern's ENGW 3302 or ENGW 3315. Official descriptions are in data/raw/neu/ (courses-2025-26-engw page).

title: Khoury Elective
description: An upper-level course chosen from the computer science, cybersecurity, or data science offerings.

title: Presentation Requirement
description: A course on speaking to an audience, such as public speaking, persuasion, or performance, that builds confidence and clarity in oral presentation.
notes: Northeastern: one course from a list of COMM and THTR courses.

title: Security Course
description: An introductory or intermediate course in computer security, such as the foundations of cybersecurity, systems security, or network security.
notes: Northeastern: one of three CY courses.

title: CS 4530 or CS 4535 (Fundamentals of Software Engineering)
description: A software engineering course in which students build a substantial system, usually in teams, using practices such as requirements, design, testing, and version control.
notes: Choice slot: Northeastern's CS 4530 or the practicum capstone CS 4535. Official descriptions are in data/raw/neu/ (courses-2025-26-cs page).
